heroHeadline: UNSC Hears Gaza Warning: 856 Killed Since October Ceasefire; Colombia 9 Days to Election as US Threatens Non-Recognition; Ukraine-Russia Both Souring on US Mediation
heroSubtitle: May 22, 2026 — The UN Security Council held its monthly open debate on the Middle East with Deputy Special Coordinator Alakbarov warning that conditions across the Occupied Palestinian Territory are 'increasingly precarious': 856 Palestinians killed by Israeli forces since the October 10, 2025 ceasefire (averaging 3+ per day under a nominal ceasefire framework), IDF controls 50%+ of Gaza, and OCHA documented 49 Israeli settler attacks in the West Bank in a single week (May 12–18). The debate also provided the first formal UNSC forum since the Board of Peace (Mladenov) on May 19–21 petitioned the Council to press Hamas to disarm — naming Hamas's refusal the 'principal obstacle' to Phase 2; Hamas counter-offered conditioning any disarmament on Palestinian statehood. In Colombia, nine days before the May 31 election, US Senator Bernie Moreno warned Washington might not recognize results if voter intimidation is documented — prompting President Petro to respond 'This is a democracy, not servitude.' Conflicting polls sharpened the runoff uncertainty: Invamer shows Cepeda at 44.6% in the first round, while Guarumo shows De la Espriella leading 43.6%–40% in a direct runoff — a gap that could determine whether Colombia's peace architecture advances or is dismantled on June 21. On Ukraine-Russia, Foreign Policy assessed that both sides are souring on US mediation, with Zelensky saying Ukraine is 'waiting on U.S. and Russia to set the next talks' and Europe (Costa) weighing a more direct role. Lebanon: Day 7 of the 45-day ceasefire extension, Pentagon security track now seven days away (May 29).
footerNote: Data sourced from UN, African Union, IGAD, Crisis Group, USIP, PA-X Database, and Tier 1–3 sources across all media poles.
